programme.displayName: Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test
programme.subtitle: sqs-learning-path · SAA-C03 beginner hands-on journey
programme.description: A beginner-focused Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) Follow Along in Europe (London) (eu-west-2). It builds practical understanding of standard queues, FIFO queues, visibility timeouts, long polling, message attributes, dead-letter queues, redrive, encryption, monitoring attributes, and SAA-C03 architecture decisions.
programme.learningOutcome: Create and test Amazon SQS standard and FIFO queues; send, receive, delay, inspect, delete, retry, and redrive harmless messages; explain queue identifiers, at-least-once delivery, ordering, dead-letter queues, encryption, and the SQS use cases most relevant to the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) exam.

tasks.title: 1. Confirm Approved SQS Access in eu-west-2
tasks.feature: Amazon SQS access and regional queue listing
tasks.goal: Confirm that an approved non-root identity can access Amazon SQS in Europe (London) and list accessible queues.
tasks.whyItMatters: Amazon SQS queues are regional. Root credentials have unrestricted account access and are not appropriate for routine work; use an organization-approved identity with temporary credentials where available. Queue URLs returned by the CLI are Region-specific.

consoleSteps.title: Open the Amazon SQS console
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in with your approved non-root identity.

instructions.text: Sign in with your approved non-root identity.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Amazon SQS console opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use the AWS account root user for this training.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab Region
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Europe (London) is selected.
consoleSteps.warning: Use eu-west-2 for every regional SQS action in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Open the queue list
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Queues page is visible in Europe (London).
consoleSteps.warning: An empty queue list is valid for a new training account.

cliSteps.explanation: Lists queue URLs that the configured approved CLI identity can access in Europe (London). Configure the CLI through your organization-approved authentication method before running this command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrls when queues are accessible, or an empty result when no queues exist.
cliSteps.warning: An AccessDenied error means the approved identity needs SQS list access; do not switch to root credentials.

verification.title: Verify Console access
verification.instruction: Confirm that the SQS Queues page remains open with Europe (London) selected.
verification.expectedResult: You can view the regional queue list.

verification.title: Verify CLI access

tasks.title: 2. Create a Standard Queue and Complete the Message Lifecycle
tasks.feature: Standard queue, queue URL, message ID, receipt handle, and message attributes
tasks.goal: Create sqs-saa-study-standard, record its identifiers, send a harmless message with an attribute, receive it, inspect it, and delete it.
tasks.whyItMatters: A Standard queue decouples producers from consumers and supports at-least-once delivery with best-effort ordering. A MessageId identifies a sent message, while the most recent ReceiptHandle is required to delete a received message.

consoleSteps.title: Create the standard queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue Details page opens for sqs-saa-study-standard.
consoleSteps.warning: Queue type cannot be changed after creation. Do not put confidential information in queue names.

consoleSteps.title: Record queue identifiers
consoleSteps.expectedResult: You have the queue URL and queue ARN for later tasks.
consoleSteps.warning: Later SQS CLI operations use the Queue URL, not the queue name.

consoleSteps.title: Send a sample message

instructions.text: Enter Study tracker standard message in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console confirms that the test message was sent and shows its Message ID.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only the fixed harmless sample data.

consoleSteps.title: Receive and delete the sample message

instructions.text: Choose Delete in the confirmation dialog.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected test message is removed from the queue.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the message whose body is Study tracker standard message.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates the standard training queue. A queue is Standard when no FIFO attribute is specified.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrl for sqs-saa-study-standard.
cliSteps.warning: If this name exists with different attributes, SQS can return an error.

cliSteps.explanation: Retrieves the queue ARN. Replace <standard-queue-url-from-create-queue> with the QueueUrl returned by the previous command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains QueueArn.
cliSteps.warning: The queue URL is account-specific.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-create-queue> --message-body "Study tracker standard message" --message-attributes '{"studyType":{"DataType":"String","StringValue":"standard-test"}}' --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends one harmless message with a String message attribute. Replace the queue URL placeholder with the URL from queue creation.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId and an MD5 digest.
cliSteps.warning: Do not substitute personal, confidential, or production data.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs receive-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-create-queue> --message-system-attribute-names All --message-attribute-names All --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Receives an available message and returns its MessageId, Body, current ReceiptHandle, system attributes, and requested message attributes.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains the sample message and a ReceiptHandle.
cliSteps.warning: Save the ReceiptHandle from this receive result; a receipt handle changes when a message is received again.

cliSteps.explanation: Permanently deletes the message returned by the immediately preceding receive-message command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Use the current ReceiptHandle, not the MessageId.

verification.title: Verify the standard queue
verification.instruction: Confirm that sqs-saa-study-standard shows Type Standard on its Details page.
verification.expectedResult: The queue is a Standard queue.

verification.title: Verify message deletion
verification.expectedResult: Study tracker standard message is not returned.

cleanup.title: Remove the completed lifecycle test message
cleanup.instruction: Confirm that Study tracker standard message was deleted before continuing.
cleanup.description: Confirm that Study tracker standard message was deleted before continuing.
cleanup.verification: Polling does not show Study tracker standard message.

tasks.title: 3. Configure Delays, Long Polling, Retention, and Visibility Timeout
tasks.feature: Message retention, delay queues, long polling, short polling, visibility timeout, and consumer retry behavior
tasks.goal: Configure safe test settings on the standard queue, send a delayed message, observe long polling, then make a received message visible again without deleting it.
tasks.whyItMatters: Retention controls how long unconsumed messages remain available. Delays buffer scheduled work for up to 15 minutes. Long polling reduces empty receives. Visibility timeout protects processing work, but a message returns for retry when a consumer crashes or does not delete it before the timeout expires.

consoleSteps.title: Configure the queue

instructions.text: Choose Days for Message retention period.
Enter 20 in Receive message wait time.
Choose Seconds for Receive message wait time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The edit form shows one-day retention, a 10-second visibility timeout, and 20-second long polling.
consoleSteps.warning: A short visibility timeout is intentional for this safe retry demonstration; production values must match expected processing time.

consoleSteps.title: Save the queue settings
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue Details page shows the saved settings.
consoleSteps.warning: Queue attribute changes can take a short time to propagate.

consoleSteps.title: Send a delayed message

instructions.text: Enter Delayed study task in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console confirms the delayed message was sent.
consoleSteps.warning: Per-message delay is supported for Standard queues and is limited to 15 minutes.

consoleSteps.title: Demonstrate a retry

instructions.text: Choose Delete in the confirmation dialog.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message becomes invisible after the first receive, returns after the visibility timeout, and is then deleted.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete the message during the first receive; the task intentionally demonstrates a consumer that did not complete processing.

cliSteps.explanation: Sets one-day retention, a 10-second visibility timeout, and 20-second queue-level long polling. Replace the placeholder with the standard queue URL.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: These settings affect only sqs-saa-study-standard when the correct Queue URL is used.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Delayed study task" --delay-seconds 10 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends a harmless Standard-queue message that becomes available after 10 seconds.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: A FIFO queue does not support a per-message delay.

cliSteps.explanation: Long-polls for the delayed message and returns its current ReceiptHandle and ApproximateReceiveCount when it becomes available.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns Delayed study task after its delay, or returns no Messages if the polling window expires first.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete the returned message yet; record its receipt handle only if you need it for investigation.

cliSteps.explanation: Ends the current invisibility period immediately so the unprocessed message can be received again. The receipt-handle placeholder comes from the preceding receive-message result.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output and the message becomes available for another consumer.
cliSteps.warning: Use only the receipt handle returned for Delayed study task.

cliSteps.explanation: Receives the visible retry and returns a new ReceiptHandle. The ApproximateReceiveCount demonstrates that the message has been received more than once.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result includes Delayed study task and an increased ApproximateReceiveCount.
cliSteps.warning: Use the newest receipt handle for deletion.

cliSteps.explanation: Deletes the retried message after the safe failure-and-retry demonstration.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: A Standard queue can still deliver a message more than once; consumers should make processing idempotent.

verification.title: Verify long polling
verification.expectedResult: Receive message wait time is 20 seconds, which enables long polling instead of the default short polling.

verification.title: Verify retry behavior
verification.expectedResult: Delayed study task has a new ReceiptHandle and an ApproximateReceiveCount greater than its first receive.

cleanup.title: Restore the standard-queue visibility timeout
cleanup.instruction: Edit sqs-saa-study-standard and set Visibility timeout to 30 Seconds.
cleanup.description: Edit sqs-saa-study-standard and set Visibility timeout to 30 Seconds.
cleanup.verification: The queue Details page shows a 30-second visibility timeout.

tasks.title: 4. Inspect Queue Backlog Attributes and Purge Test Messages
tasks.feature: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible, ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage, and purge behavior
tasks.goal: Create a small safe backlog, inspect SQS approximate queue attributes, and purge only training messages from the standard queue.
tasks.whyItMatters: SQS queue depth and age indicate whether workers are keeping up. Visible messages indicate backlog, not-visible messages indicate in-flight work, and age of the oldest message can indicate slow consumers. These measurements guide worker capacity and SQS-driven Auto Scaling decisions.

consoleSteps.title: Create a small test backlog

instructions.text: Enter Backlog test message one in Message body.
Enter Backlog test message two in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Two harmless backlog messages have been sent.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use purge on a shared or production queue.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect queue monitoring data
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The monitoring view provides queue activity and backlog information.
consoleSteps.warning: SQS counts are approximate because SQS is distributed.

consoleSteps.title: Purge only the training queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The training queue is emptied of its backlog test messages.
consoleSteps.warning: Purging deletes all messages in the selected queue. Perform this only on sqs-saa-study-standard.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Backlog test message one" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Adds the first harmless backlog message to the standard training queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: Use only the queue created by this Follow Along.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Backlog test message two" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Adds the second harmless backlog message to the standard training queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: Do not send production data.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage NumberOfMessagesSent NumberOfMessagesReceived NumberOfMessagesDeleted --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Returns approximate visible, in-flight, and oldest-message values along with available message operation counters.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains requested queue attributes when available.
cliSteps.warning: Approximate attributes should be used as indicators rather than exact transaction counts.

cliSteps.explanation: Removes all messages from the standard training queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: This permanently removes every message in the specified queue. Use only sqs-saa-study-standard.

verification.title: Verify queue backlog metrics
verification.instruction: Review the requested queue attributes before purging.
verification.expectedResult: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible indicates that messages were available for workers.

verification.title: Verify the purge
verification.expectedResult: Backlog test messages are not returned.

cleanup.title: Confirm backlog messages are removed
cleanup.verification: Backlog test message one and Backlog test message two are not returned.

tasks.title: 5. Create and Test a FIFO Queue
tasks.feature: FIFO naming, strict ordering within a message group, message group IDs, deduplication IDs, and content-based deduplication
tasks.goal: Create sqs-saa-study-orders.fifo, send ordered messages in one message group, and compare FIFO behavior with the Standard queue.
tasks.whyItMatters: Use FIFO when strict ordering and deduplication are required. FIFO queue names must end in .fifo. Ordering is preserved within each MessageGroupId, allowing separate message groups to be processed independently.

consoleSteps.title: Create the FIFO queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The FIFO queue Details page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: The .fifo suffix is mandatory and the queue type cannot be changed after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Send ordered FIFO messages

instructions.text: Enter Order step one in Message body.
Enter study-order-001 in Message group ID.
Enter Order step two in Message body.
Enter study-order-001 in Message group ID.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Two messages are accepted for the same FIFO message group.
consoleSteps.warning: FIFO queues require a Message group ID. Per-message delivery delay is not supported for FIFO queues.

consoleSteps.title: Receive and delete FIFO messages

instructions.text: Choose Delete in the confirmation dialog.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Order step one is processed before Order step two for the same message group.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the fixed FIFO test messages.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates a FIFO queue with content-based deduplication enabled.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrl for sqs-saa-study-orders.fifo.
cliSteps.warning: A FIFO queue name must end in .fifo.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <fifo-queue-url-from-create-queue> --message-body "Order step one" --message-group-id study-order-001 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends the first ordered message. Content-based deduplication means no explicit deduplication ID is required for this queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns MessageId and SequenceNumber.
cliSteps.warning: Replace the placeholder with the FIFO QueueUrl returned by the create-queue command.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <fifo-queue-url-from-create-queue> --message-body "Order step two" --message-group-id study-order-001 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends the second message in the same FIFO message group.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns MessageId and SequenceNumber.
cliSteps.warning: The shared MessageGroupId is what makes ordering relevant for these two messages.

cliSteps.explanation: Receives the next available FIFO message and returns its current ReceiptHandle and MessageGroupId system attribute.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result returns Order step one before Order step two for this message group.
cliSteps.warning: Do not request a later message in the same group until the earlier message is deleted or becomes visible again.

cliSteps.explanation: Deletes the first FIFO message, allowing the next message in that message group to be processed.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Use the latest ReceiptHandle.

verification.title: Verify FIFO identity
verification.instruction: Confirm that the queue name ends in .fifo and the queue Type is FIFO.
verification.expectedResult: sqs-saa-study-orders.fifo is displayed as a FIFO queue.

verification.title: Verify FIFO send result
verification.expectedResult: Each result includes a SequenceNumber, which is returned for FIFO messages.

cleanup.title: Delete the remaining FIFO test message
cleanup.instruction: Poll the FIFO queue and delete Order step two.
cleanup.description: Poll the FIFO queue and delete Order step two.
cleanup.verification: Order step two is not returned by a subsequent poll.

tasks.title: 6. Configure a Dead-Letter Queue and Redrive a Poison Message
tasks.feature: Dead-letter queue, redrive policy, maxReceiveCount, failed messages, poison messages, and message redrive
tasks.goal: Create sqs-saa-study-dlq, attach it to the standard queue with maxReceiveCount of 2, deliberately fail one harmless message, inspect it in the DLQ, and redrive it.
tasks.whyItMatters: A dead-letter queue isolates poison messages that repeatedly fail processing. A redrive policy defines the DLQ and maxReceiveCount. For SAA-C03, use DLQs to protect consumers from repeated failures while preserving failed work for diagnosis and controlled retry.

consoleSteps.title: Create the dead-letter queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The sqs-saa-study-dlq Details page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: A source queue and its DLQ must be in the same account and Region.

consoleSteps.title: Configure the source queue redrive policy
consoleSteps.expectedResult: sqs-saa-study-standard has a redrive policy targeting sqs-saa-study-dlq after two failed receives.
consoleSteps.warning: Use a small maxReceiveCount only for this controlled lab. Production retry counts must allow sufficient time for transient failures.

consoleSteps.title: Move a poison-message test to the DLQ

instructions.text: Enter Poison study task in Message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message is received without deletion until it exceeds the configured receive count and is moved to the DLQ.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete Poison study task from the source queue during this demonstration.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect and redrive the DLQ message
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The failed message is visible in the DLQ and a redrive task is started to move it back to the source queue.
consoleSteps.warning: Redrive moves messages asynchronously. The destination queue must be the same queue type as the DLQ.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name sqs-saa-study-dlq --attributes MessageRetentionPeriod=172800 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates a Standard DLQ with two-day message retention. A DLQ should retain messages longer than its source queue where practical.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns QueueUrl for sqs-saa-study-dlq.
cliSteps.warning: Replace none of the harmless fixed queue names with production queue names.

cliSteps.explanation: Gets the DLQ ARN needed by the source queue redrive policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains the DLQ QueueArn.
cliSteps.warning: Replace the placeholder with the DLQ QueueUrl from the preceding create-queue result.

cliSteps.explanation: Associates the standard queue with the DLQ. Replace the DLQ ARN placeholder with the QueueArn returned by the preceding command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: This changes the redrive policy on sqs-saa-study-standard only.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --message-body "Poison study task" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sends one harmless test message that will intentionally not be deleted by the consumer.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete this message until it reaches the DLQ.

cliSteps.explanation: Receives the poison-message test and immediately ends its invisibility so it can be received again without waiting. Repeat this single command once more only after the first response returns.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns Poison study task and leaves it visible again for another receive attempt.
cliSteps.warning: The task intentionally simulates an unsuccessful consumer. A message moves to the DLQ only after its receive count exceeds maxReceiveCount.

cliSteps.explanation: Checks the DLQ after the failed receives. Replace the placeholder with the DLQ QueueUrl.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result returns Poison study task after SQS moves it to the DLQ.
cliSteps.warning: SQS propagation and message movement can take a short time; repeat this receive request if no message is returned initially.

cliSteps.explanation: Starts asynchronous redrive from the DLQ to its configured source queue. Replace the placeholder with the DLQ ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns an identifier for the message movement task.
cliSteps.warning: Redrive requires the caller to have the required SQS permissions on the DLQ and destination queue; encrypted queues also require KMS permissions.

verification.title: Verify DLQ configuration
verification.instruction: Open sqs-saa-study-standard Details and inspect the dead-letter queue configuration.
verification.expectedResult: The redrive policy identifies sqs-saa-study-dlq and maxReceiveCount 2.

verification.title: Verify the redrive task
verification.expectedResult: The result identifies an asynchronous message move task.

cleanup.title: Delete the redriven poison-message test
cleanup.instruction: Receive Poison study task from sqs-saa-study-standard and delete it using its current receipt handle.
cleanup.description: Receive Poison study task from sqs-saa-study-standard and delete it using its current receipt handle.
cleanup.verification: Poison study task is not returned from the source queue or DLQ.

tasks.title: 7. Apply SAA-C03 SQS Architecture Decisions
tasks.feature: Decoupled workers, traffic-spike buffering, Lambda, EC2 workers, Auto Scaling, SNS fan-out, EventBridge routing, encryption, queue policies, and large-message patterns
tasks.goal: Use the configured queues and observed queue attributes to choose the correct SQS-based architecture for common SAA-C03 scenarios.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam tests service choice and integration behavior. SQS is a pull-based durable buffer for asynchronous workers; SNS is pub/sub fan-out; EventBridge routes events by rules. Lambda polls SQS in batches, and queue backlog signals can drive worker scaling.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect encryption and permissions options
consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can identify the queue encryption and access-policy configuration areas.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add a public, cross-account, or broad queue policy in this training account. Service integrations require narrowly scoped permissions that must be reviewed by the account administrator.

consoleSteps.title: Review the Lambda queue design

instructions.text: Identify the queue visibility timeout guidance.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can explain that Lambda polls SQS and that queue visibility timeout must accommodate Lambda retries.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create a Lambda function or execution role in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Review service-selection cases

instructions.text: Find the Amazon SQS comparison column.
Find the Amazon SNS comparison column.
Find the Amazon EventBridge comparison column.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can compare pull-based queues, pub/sub fan-out, and event-rule routing.
consoleSteps.warning: Use a queue for durable worker buffering, an SNS topic for fan-out delivery, and EventBridge for event matching and routing.

cliSteps.explanation: Retrieves the queue configuration and approximate attributes needed to reason about visibility timeout, retention, long polling, encryption-related configuration, redrive policy, and queue policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result includes configured queue attributes such as VisibilityTimeout, MessageRetentionPeriod, ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds, RedrivePolicy, and QueueArn when set.
cliSteps.warning: Review a Policy attribute for unintended broad access; do not alter the policy in this training task.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url <standard-queue-url-from-task-2> --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Retrieves the approximate queue-backlog indicators used by worker-capacity and Auto Scaling designs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains the requested approximate attributes when values are available.
cliSteps.warning: These values are approximate and should be combined with application throughput and failure metrics when designing scaling.

verification.title: Verify SAA-C03 scenario decisions
verification.instruction: State the service choice for each case: asynchronous worker backlog, one event to multiple independent consumers, rule-based event routing, strict ordering, and a slow backend during a traffic spike.
verification.expectedResult: Use SQS for asynchronous buffering and workers; SNS for fan-out; EventBridge for event-rule routing; FIFO SQS for ordered groups; and queue backlog metrics for worker scaling decisions.

verification.title: Verify Lambda reliability reasoning
verification.instruction: State the relationship between Lambda timeout and the SQS visibility timeout.
verification.expectedResult: The queue visibility timeout is at least six times the Lambda function timeout when Lambda consumes the queue.

cleanup.title: Leave architecture-review resources unchanged
cleanup.instruction: Do not create or change Lambda, SNS, S3, EventBridge, EC2, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, KMS, or queue-policy resources in this task.

warnings.cost: Amazon SQS requests and related services can incur charges. This Follow Along creates three small SQS queues and uses only small harmless messages. Delete all three named queues after verification.
warnings.safety: Use only the fixed queue names and fixed harmless sample messages. Never place personal, confidential, regulated, or production data in queue names or message bodies. Do not purge, delete, or edit any queue that was not created by this Follow Along.
warnings.credentials: Do not create, expose, download, paste, or share credentials. Use only an organization-approved non-root authentication method and follow local identity-management procedures.
warnings.region: Perform all regional Amazon SQS operations in Europe (London), eu-west-2. Queue URLs, ARNs, queue policies, and integrations are Region-specific.

findings.message: The requested first lab requires creating an IAM user, assigning permissions, creating CLI credentials, and configuring those credentials. This replacement deliberately does not include IAM-user creation, credential creation, access-key handling, or IAM policy content because the controlling instructions prohibit credentials and IAM policies. The first task instead verifies access using an already approved non-root identity.

The requested SQS integrations with Lambda, SNS, S3, EventBridge, EC2, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, KMS, and cross-account queues require service-specific IAM roles, resource policies, and sometimes account-level configuration. The controlling instructions prohibit proposing IAM policies, so this package provides documented architecture and verification guidance rather than creating those dependent resources.

No official AWS documentation source returned by the protected search was used to support a complete hands-on Kinesis comparison lab. The architecture comparison task therefore covers SQS, SNS, and EventBridge from the official AWS decision guide and leaves Kinesis out rather than guessing implementation details.

Before publishing, manually verify that the current AWS Management Console exposes the exact dead-letter queue redrive control label shown for the account and Region. The CLI redrive operation is documented and included separately.
